title: Redis vs Dragonfly: A Hands-On Comparison
why_read: A hands-on practical comparison of Redis against the newer Dragonfly database, covering real workload testing and architectural reasoning, offers useful, grounded information for backend engineers.
analysis: This post compares Redis, the ubiquitous in-memory data store, against Dragonfly, a newer alternative that keeps the same API but uses a different internal architecture, reportedly multi-threaded rather than Redis's traditional single-threaded design. The author ran both under the same workload and reports firsthand observations rather than just repeating vendor marketing, which adds credibility. It explains why Redis's simple command model and single-threaded design made it fast in the first place, setting up a reasonable comparison point. This is a solid, grounded piece for backend engineers evaluating caching and data store options, though it is a single blog's informal benchmark rather than a rigorous study.
